knowledge.body_en:
A corporate bond's yield is the risk-free rate plus a spread. The spread is the market's price for default and liquidity risk. With the US 10-year near 5%, a coupon around 10% implies a spread of roughly 500 basis points, squarely in high-yield territory (rated below BBB-). Spreads widen when investors fear defaults and tighten when they chase yield.

Order books tell the other half of the story. Demand at twice the issue size means investors will fund aggressive AI capex at that price, even as better-rated AI issuers lean on convertibles instead. Watch whether spreads stay tight as issuance grows; widening would be the first sign the AI financing cycle is cooling.
knowledge.why_en: SoftBank's jumbo junk bond, reportedly priced near 10% against a 4.97% Treasury, is the clearest live read on AI-capex financing risk.
